24: PETER. Help me in. [ Stops ] Nikíta!
22: MATRYÓNA [ runs up into the porch and holds Peter up ] Shall I help you into the hut?
20: PETER. Else … o-oh! when the time comes for planting, they'll all be rotten. Oh, I can't stand it! [ Rises ].
18: ANÍSYA [ aside ] No fear, I'm not going. He's again sending every one away; he must have the money on him now, and wants to hide it somewhere.
17: PETER. Well then—o-oh!… Get out the seed potatoes, and the women will go and sort them.
15: MATRYÓNA [ approaches ] Oh, sonnie, why don't you take more pains for your master? Your master is ill and depends on you; you should serve him as you would your own father, straining every muscle just as I always tell you to.
14: PETER. Too far? From here it's still farther. You'll have to go on purpose now. You might have made one job of it. [ Anísya, without showing herself, stands and listens ].
13: NIKÍTA. It's too far to go there.
11: PETER. Have you done the strip beyond the bridge?
8: PETER. Why have you come back so early?
6: PETER [ opens his eyes ] Nikíta, I say, Nikíta, come here! [ Nikíta approaches. Anísya and Matryóna whisper together ].
5: NIKÍTA. Well, let him sit. What's it to me?
4: MATRYÓNA. Hush, there he sits. [ Points to porch ].
1: MATRYÓNA. The Lord be thanked, we're all alive and have a crust to bite.
0: ANÍSYA. Just on the boil. NIKÍTA [ comes from the other side, if possible on horseback, up to the gate, and does not see Peter. To Matryóna ] How d'you do, mother, is all well at home?
